cues: During furniture assembly, a hand tool turns threaded fasteners until the joined panels sit firmly together.
A repairer applies steady torque to a small metal fastener, tightening a hinge without damaging its threads.
The technician rotates a handled tool clockwise, drawing a loose bracket snug against the wooden frame.
In a workshop, a replaceable tip seats into a recessed fastener before careful turns secure the casing.
A cabinet hinge is adjusted by loosening its threaded mounting points, shifting the door, then tightening them again.
To open the appliance cover, the mechanic turns each slotted fastener and keeps the small parts organized.
The installer checks a fastener's fit, then makes short controlled turns until the wall fixture stops wobbling.
During routine maintenance, applying torque to threaded hardware helps keep joints tight and equipment stable.
